Medical History

- Current health issues and chronic disease risk factors:
  - Acute exacerbation of asthma-like symptoms over 2–3 days: shortness of breath with exertion, wheeze, cough; no scheduled results provided.
  - Inhaled corticosteroid therapy ongoing (brown inhaler discussed; dose adjustments recommended).
  - Peak flow historically around 380 (previous baseline; unit not specified).
  - No history of hospital admission for asthma; last major asthma attack 3–4 years ago.
  - Hay fever reported as allergy; patient initially stated fever but corrected to hay fever (conflict noted).

- Family history of chronic conditions:
  - Brother with asthma.
  - Sister with eczema.

- Current medications including OTC and traditional medicines:
  - Salbutamol inhaler (blue) – used as needed; described as being used daily for prevention; interim plan allows use every 2–4 hours; dose/route/frequency not fully documented.
  - Brown inhaler (Clenil) – beclomethasone inhaler; plan to increase from 3 puffs twice daily to 4 puffs twice daily.
  - Cetraben (emollient) and Hydrocortisone (topical steroid) – for skin/eczema management.
  - Bactroban-containing topical (mentioned as Flanel Bactroban) – dose/route/frequency not documented.

Recommendation for documentation and next steps (informational only; not part of the formal note):
- Obtain formal asthma review with GP within 3–7 days.
- Consider formal asthma action plan based on peak flow and symptom control.
- Schedule chest examination with peak flow measurement during next visit; consider antibiotics or oral steroids if indicated by exam/flow results.
- Confirm and reconcile medication names/doses (especially inhaled corticosteroid dose and topical therapies).
- Update immunisation status and address any preventive care gaps (flu, COVID-19, pneumococcal, shingles, tetanus).
- Document vital signs, anthropometrics, and relevant laboratory tests as soon as available.
- Assess for social determinants of health and consider referrals if needed.
